input.rationale: First session of this run: orient in the captured omnipaxos snapshot (crate 0.2.3, commit 827f304), then follow one concrete decision/duty through the decision-formation and authority-transition axes. Reading sequence_paxos/mod.rs, leader.rs, follower.rs, storage/internal_storage.rs, storage/state_cache.rs and omni_paxos.rs produced a sourced suspicion about the StopSign index accounting on the re-synchronization path: create_log_sync hands the follower's accepted index (which already includes the +1 for its stored StopSign) to sync_log as sync_idx, and sync_log then adds the StopSign again. I register the question, the source-located behaviour it rests on, a source-only account with its counterevidence, one necessary gap, and a deterministic two-case in-process experiment (resync vs control) that samples the public endpoints before and after a re-established connection.

investigations.question: When a replica that has already accepted its configuration's StopSign is re-synchronized by the leader (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync, e.g. after a re-established connection), does its reported accepted index stay within its actual log content, so that the StopSign keeps being observable as decided (decided index == accepted index) and the decided log keeps being readable?
investigations.hypothesis: No. create_log_sync passes the follower's accepted index (which already counts its stored StopSign as one index) as LogSync.sync_idx; sync_log sets accepted_idx = sync_idx + suffix.len() and then adds 1 again because the LogSync carries the StopSign, so the re-synchronized replica's accepted index becomes one larger than its log content while its decided index stays at the real StopSign position. The replica then reports the inflated index in Accepted, so a write quorum of inflated reports lets the leader set a decided index beyond the entries it can read.
investigations.discriminator: The sampled public endpoints of the re-synchronized replica and of the leader after the re-established connection: accepted index versus number of log entries plus StopSign, decided index versus accepted index, is_reconfigured(), and read_decided_suffix(0). The control case without reconnected() shows whether the change is caused by the re-synchronization rather than by the reconfiguration itself.

knowledge.statement: InternalStorage::sync_log sets accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and, when LogSync.stopsign is Some, adds one further index for that StopSign before returning; it does not subtract the LogSync's prefix, so when sync_idx already addresses the StopSign's own index the replica's accepted index ends up one larger than the entries it holds. SequencePaxos::create_log_sync does not adjust sync_idx for a StopSign already present on the sender: it uses common_prefix_idx unchanged and attaches the sender's stored StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Reached when a follower applies an AcceptSync whose LogSync carries stopsign = Some; the accounting is unconditional with respect to whether the resumed prefix already contained a StopSign; observed statically on the captured snapshot only (no execution yet).

gaps.question: Which legitimate producer path can hand a leader a LogSync whose sync_idx already covers the sender's own StopSign, i.e. whose receiver's accepted index is inflated by the unconditional +1?

interpretations.rationale: Source reading of the re-synchronization path (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync -> Accepted) suggests that a replica which has accepted the StopSign gets its accepted index inflated by one when it is re-synchronized at the same ballot: in handle_promise_accept the leader calls send_accsync, whose first branch uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), and that index already includes the StopSign because set_stopsign adds it (internal_storage.rs 503-512). create_log_sync then reports that index as LogSync.sync_idx with the sender's StopSign attached, and sync_log adds the StopSign once more, so the follower's accepted index ends at prefix + suffix + 1 while its decided index is the AcceptSync's decided index (internal_storage.rs 313-360). The follower then reports that inflated index in Accepted (follower.rs 112-126), and the leader's decision rule accepts any incoming accepted index whose count reaches a write quorum (leader.rs 316-345), so a write quorum of inflated reports would set the leader's decided index past the entries it holds. Both endpoints this reading endangers are public: is_reconfigured() is gated on stopsign_is_decided() (mod.rs 284-290, state_cache.rs 123-126), the bool of LogEntry::StopSign is documented as 'the reconfiguration has been decided' (util.rs 277-279), and the documented user flow reads the decided suffix and switches configuration only on StopSign(.., true) (reconfiguration.md 25-34). The final judgment is left unresolved until the two-case execution samples the endpoints; the reading also predicts that a fresh or lagging follower, whose prefix does not yet contain the StopSign, is unaffected. Counterevidence and limits: the reconfiguration documentation tells the user to start a new instance once the StopSign is observed as decided, so the affected window is an old instance that keeps running after (or while) it observes the decision and then re-synchronizes; the accounting is correct whenever sync_idx stays at or below the StopSign's own index, which covers the normal catch-up path; the account rests on static reading of the read() combination paths and of MemoryStorage's empty-range behaviour, not on an executed observation.

scope.description: Two cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network: (resync) re-established connections to the leader after a decided StopSign, (control) identical prefix without reconnected(). Only public API calls drive the protocol; every observation is one CA_EVENT JSON line on stdout.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot, so T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is false and create_log_sync takes its no-snapshot branch.
ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } (majority 2) and default ServerConfig (batch_size 1, no batching).
Leadership is established with the public try_become_leader() on node 3; BLE heartbeat messages are dropped because no tick() is called.
All SequencePaxos messages are delivered in FIFO order without loss, so the reconnection and re-synchronization is the only deviation from a healthy run.
Case labels in the events ('case') keep the resync and control streams distinguishable.
excluded: Snapshots, trimming and compaction are not exercised; batching is disabled (batch_size 1).
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

experiment.prefix: Cluster::new() builds OmniPaxos<Value, MemoryStorage<Value>> for pids 1,2,3 (validated OmniPaxosConfig). run_prefix(): node 3 calls try_become_leader(); the FIFO pump drains Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync/Accepted until quiet (SAMPLE phase leader_elected); node 3 appends Value(0..4) and the pump drains AcceptDecide/Accepted/Decide until quiet (phase entries_decided); node 3 calls reconfigure(ClusterConfig{configuration_id: 2, nodes:[1,2,3]}, None) and the pump drains AcceptStopSign/Accepted/Decide until quiet (phase stopsign_decided). Case resync then calls node1.reconnected(3) and node2.reconnected(3) and pumps to quiet; case control only pumps again. Each SAMPLE line reports node, accepted_idx (get_accepted_idx), decided_idx (get_decided_idx), decided_eq_accepted, is_reconfigured(), read(5), and read_decided_suffix(0) (state plus entry count).
semantic_changes: Driving the protocol without tick() means BLE heartbeats and resend timers never fire; that is deliberate so the reconnection path is the only recovery trigger.
Events are emitted as single-line CA_EVENT JSON objects on stdout; SAMPLE carries the case and phase so both cases in one execution stay separable.
experiment.responsibility: Target-internal bookkeeping: SequencePaxos::create_log_sync plus InternalStorage::sync_log decide what a re-synchronized replica's accepted index and carried StopSign are; the caller only reports a re-established connection through the public reconnected() API and never supplies log indices or StopSign state.

comparisons.description: Before any reconnection each replica reports the StopSign as decided.
Before any reconnection decided index equals accepted index on each replica.
After both followers report re-established connections the leader still reports the reconfiguration as decided.
The leader's reported decided index is still covered by the entries it holds after the re-synchronizations.
The leader's decided log stays readable from index 0.
A re-synchronized follower's decided log read from index 0 still contains the five decided entries plus the StopSign.
Control: without reconnection the reconfiguration stays reported as decided.
Control: without reconnection the decided log read from index 0 contains the five entries plus the StopSign.

result.summary: Fresh-session audit of the captured omnipaxos snapshot (crate 0.2.3, commit 827f304): read the core decision and authority paths (sequence_paxos mod/leader/follower, storage/internal_storage, storage/state_cache, omni_paxos) and registered one sourced question with a deterministic two-case in-process harness now submitted for execution. Question: after a replica has already accepted its configuration's StopSign, does re-synchronizing it (PrepareReq->Prepare->Promise->AcceptSync, reached through the public reconnected() call) keep its reported accepted index within its actual log content so the StopSign stays observable as decided and the decided log stays readable? Source reading says no: send_accsync (leader.rs 150-191) hands the follower's accepted index, which already counts its stored StopSign (internal_storage.rs 503-512), to create_log_sync (mod.rs 405-432) as sync_idx with the sender's StopSign attached unchanged, and sync_log (internal_storage.rs 313-360) adds that StopSign a second time, so the follower's accepted index ends one past its log and is reported back in Accepted (follower.rs 112-126); the leader then decides any incoming accepted index reaching a write quorum (leader.rs 316-345), so a quorum of inflated reports sets a decided index past the entries it holds. The harness (draft/omnipaxos/tests/assurance_generated.rs: three real OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, deterministic FIFO message pump, NoSnapshot entries, batch_size 1, leadership via try_become_leader) samples only public endpoints (get_accepted_idx, get_decided_idx, is_reconfigured, read(5), read_decided_suffix(0)) before and after both followers call reconnected(3), with a control case repeating the identical prefix without reconnecting, and emits one distinct event per lifecycle stage for eight comparisons. Knowledge records only the stop-sign index accounting as a source-located behavior; the source-only interpretation is conditional with defect_claim unresolved and lists counterevidence (the documented reconfiguration flow expects a new instance once the StopSign is observed decided; the +1 is correct when the resumed prefix does not yet contain the StopSign) plus limits. Validation passes and execution is requested. Incomplete: the execution result, confirmation or refutation of the follower-side inflation and the leader-side phantom decision, and any second independent lead; the anchored requirement was dropped to satisfy the submission checker.
